correctness.rationale: Binary indicator vertices have maximum squared Euclidean distance exactly N only at complementary pairs; both all-vertex and all-edge covers exist for n>=3. For fixed red-vertex set A, within-class edges are forced opposite, crossing edges are independent, and only singleton A or its complement has one forbidden monochromatic star per choice. Exhaustive n=3,4,5 enumeration independently confirms every layer. The central-binomial ratio product gives an absolutely summable O(1/n) theta-weight error plus negligible singleton correction; after normalization this proves total variation O(1/n). The finite verifier is not used as an infinite proof.

originality.rationale: The full primary arXiv HTML manuscript (sections 1, 2.1, 4, 5) gives the covering polytope, domination equivalence and facet inequalities, but does not enumerate Euclidean diametral vertex pairs, the exceptional one-vertex obstruction, or the theta limits. Searches under incidence-graph domination, complementary dominating sets and metric polytope terminology produced non-implying results. A standard binary-cube diameter bound is prior elementary geometry and not claimed as new. No proof of historical uniqueness is asserted.
residual_risks: Historical priority remains provisional: an unindexed or differently named enumeration of 2-domatic partitions of a once-subdivided complete graph could give some or all exact counts.
Disjoint-domination literature beyond readable abstracts has not been exhaustively examined; no absence of earlier proof is certified.

The theta law is a consequence of a fresh combinatorial sum using standard discrete Laplace estimates; standardity of the asymptotic technique does not imply a prior theorem on this specific polytope.

value.rationale: An all-dimensional exact classification and enumerator for the Euclidean diametral vertex pairs of a freshly introduced nontrivial polytope family; sharp cardinality-one exceptions and an order-one parity-dependent theta fluctuation law provide structural information not available from the tautological cube diameter bound. The metric index and random extremizer layer are natural for comparing the size and location of all extremal pairs; no general-polytope theorem is falsely claimed.
